html:
A mathematician and physicist from Basra who did his main work in Cairo under the Fatimid caliphate. His Book of Optics showed that we see because light from objects enters the eye, and it put careful experiment at the centre of science.

A famous story says he offered to control the Nile floods. The caliph al-Hakim called him to Cairo, he saw that the plan was impossible, and he pretended to be mad until the caliph died. In the meantime he wrote the Book of Optics, in seven volumes.

Greek thinkers had argued over whether the eye sends out rays. Ibn al-Haytham showed it receives them, and he studied reflection, refraction and the camera obscura. He insisted that ideas be tested by controlled, repeatable experiments, which is why many see him as a pioneer of the scientific method. He also wrote doubts about the astronomy of Ptolemy. Translated into Latin around 1200, his optics shaped Roger Bacon and later Johannes Kepler.
